pages.lesson:
LESSON: POETRY WRITING – SPOKEN WORD

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: THEATRE AND FILM FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Creating
Topic 1.3: Poetry writing – Spoken word
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Poetry writing – Spoken word, part of Creating in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 THEATRE AND FILM FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How can Spoken word poetry be used to address issues affecting society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Poetry writing – Spoken word together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: the learner acquires innovation skills through writing original poems.

● Communication and collaboration: the learner develops proficiency in language use when writing poems.

● Learning to Learn: the learner acquires new knowledge and skills relevant for continued learning in the course of poetry

writing.

Values:
● Integrity: the learner develops honesty through creation of own works of poetry.

● Patriotism: the learner develops a sense of love for family, community and the country when writing poetry on societal

issues.

● Social Justice: the learner acquires a sense of humaneness by exploring issues affecting the society.

11

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Socio-economic and Environmental Issues: the learner becomes aware of issues affecting society while exploring themes

for writing poetry

● Peer Education and Mentorship: the learner acquires leadership and group dynamics skills during peer review.

Suggested learning resources

● Sample recorded spoken word poems

● Digital devices with assistive technologies

● Textbooks in print and in braille

Key skills to be assessed

Composing a spoken word poem using poetic elements theme, persona, form, and language, word play, rhyme patterns to

convey the intended message

12
